cards.explanation: The first thing the LORD tells Solomon is that He has heard his prayer. He says, “I have heard your prayer…” (2 Chronicles 7:12). Solomon, Israel's king, had prayed at the temple, and the first thing he hears is that he was heard. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, friends, so I can tell you that hits different.

The answer is sacrifice. The LORD says, “…have chosen this place for Myself as a house of sacrifice.” That's how He describes the temple Solomon built. It's the LORD who says He chose it, friends, and that's what makes this place so special.

The answer is to humble themselves and seek Him. That's the heart of it. The LORD says, “…if My people who are called by My name humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven…” The hard days could be no rain, locusts or a plague, and the answer is the same: come to Him. I find humbling myself is easy right up until I have to do it.

The answer is heal. The LORD says, “…then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.” That's three promises in one sentence, friends. He has just talked about the sky closing, locusts or a plague, so I think a land in trouble would be glad to hear it (2 Chronicles 7:13).

The answer is True. The LORD says, “My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.” He also says He has chosen and consecrated this temple so that His Name may be there forever (2 Chronicles 7:16). Solomon, Israel's king, heard this at night, once the temple and palace were finished. That's a promise worth hearing twice, friends.

The answer is throne. The LORD says, “…then I will establish your royal throne, as I covenanted with your father David…” David was Solomon's father and king of Israel before him (1 Kings 2:12). The promise comes with a condition: Solomon walks before the LORD as David walked. I bet that's a lot of pressure for one man, friends.

The answer is to serve and worship other gods. The LORD warns, “But if you turn away and forsake the statutes and commandments I have set before you, and if you go off to serve and worship other gods…” (2 Chronicles 7:19). Turning away from His commands and going off to other gods are put right next to each other. It's the other side of the promise to Solomon, Israel's king.

The answer is that He will uproot them from their land. The LORD says, “…then I will uproot Israel from the soil I have given them…” (2 Chronicles 7:20). I think this is a heavy part, friends. Still, it comes with a clear warning, spoken to Solomon, Israel's king, ahead of time.

The answer is False. The LORD says all who pass by will be “appalled” and will ask, “…‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’” (2 Chronicles 7:21). Nobody walks by without noticing. I think that's a heavy picture, friends.
